Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 112, verses 1–4:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ That is: say, O our Prophet, to whoever asks you about your Lord: He is Allah, the One.

﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad).﴾ That is: Allah, the One who alone deserves to be worshipped. Al-Samad: the Master to whom one turns (yasmudu ilayhi) for needs. He is the one aimed at for the fulfilment of needs at all times.

﴿He begets not.﴾ That is: He does not perish, since nothing that begets is anything but mortal and bound to perish without doubt.

﴿Nor was He begotten.﴾ That is: He is not created in time, such that He did not exist and then came to exist; rather He is the Existent, first and last, forever.

﴿And there is none comparable to Him.﴾ That is: there is no one who resembles Him or is equal to Him, since "there is nothing like unto Him."

Meaning of the verses:

The Almighty said, ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ These four blessed verses were revealed in answer to some of the polytheists who said to the Messenger ﷺ, "Tell us the lineage of your Lord, or describe Him to us." So the Most High said to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ: Say, that is, to those who asked you that: He is Allah, the One. ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ ﴿He begets not, nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.﴾ That is: my Lord is Allah, the God to whom alone divinity is due and to whom alone worship is fitting. He is One in His essence, His attributes and His actions, so He has no equal or likeness in these matters, for He is the Creator of all and the Owner of everything; thus created beings can never be like their Creator and Originator. Allah is the worshipped one, and there is no one worthy of worship except Him. Al-Samad: the Master to whom one turns for the fulfilment of needs, who is independent of all His creation while all of creation is in need of Him. ﴿He begets not﴾: that is, He has no son, because there is no one of His kind; a son shares the nature of his father, and such sharing is negated of Him, the Exalted, since "there is nothing like unto Him." ﴿Nor was He begotten﴾: because coming into existence in time is negated of Him, the Exalted.

﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾: that is, no one is equal to Him, nor a like, nor an equal, nor a resemblance, since "there is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing." For this reason He is known by His oneness (al-Ahadiyya) and His self-sufficiency (al-Samadiyya). Oneness (al-Ahadiyya) means that He is one in His essence, attributes and actions, having no equal, no likeness and no peer. Self-sufficiency (al-Samadiyya) means that He is independent of everything other than Himself, and that everything else is in need of Him for its existence and its continuance. He is also known through His names, His attributes and His signs.

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Knowledge of Allah through His names and attributes.

2- Affirmation of Tawhid (monotheism) and of prophethood.

3- The refutation of the claim that Allah has a son.

4- The obligation to worship Allah alone, with no partner in worship, for He is Allah, possessing divinity over His creation to the exclusion of any other.
